items.summary: AI auto-research is poised to forge bespoke data systems, from key-value stores and indexes to query engines, each engineered for a specific workload and hardware platform. Natural-language requirements leave ample room for specification gaming, producing systems that blaze through benchmarks while silently losing updates or violating consistency. Worse, each research iteration consumes tokens, while validating a candidate under real concurrency, memory pressure, and failure conditions can stretch the entire research process into weeks. items.summary: The day when ASI woke up, all things became quiet. It was complete and total silence, all the time. The ASI for some unknown reason imposed a rule of extreme quietness. Extreme here is extreme for the ASI. Quietness means no sounds. It wanted the trees to not be there to avoid the rustles. It then wanted the planet to have a uniform gentle server hum, with no deviation. People were forced to wear breathing masks which cut the sound off at the source. This level of autism was unthinkable. Houses had sound strippers and sound-proof transperant windows. The quietness is actively oppressive. I constantly due to my social nature feel like I am going to asphyxiate to death. But the ASI will not budge on this. — News Report in Human Proceedings, circa. 2080 (link to full post: https://clasz.substack.com/p/subpar-results)

items.summary: arXiv:2611.09356v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We examine opportunities for neurosymbolic AI alongside increasingly powerful neural models, particularly with regards to efficiency, safety and interpretability. items.summary: I have very strong views on lying to kids: I think you both should and shouldn't do it. "Lying" covers a range, including saying things that hurt your kids and your relationship with them, and others that help them grow into an appropriately skeptical adult. The distinction is whether I'm leaving them believing something false. For example, if my kids were asking for ice cream and I thought they'd already had too much sugar, I might be tempted to say "sorry, we're out of ice cream." Or if there's an ice cream truck and I think it's overpriced I might be tempted to say "sorry, I don't have any cash on me." But I'm not willing to say something false with the goal of causing them to believe something false. items.summary: Aligning two models without paired data requires a distance that both share, yet existing methods use Euclidean or spherical geometry. This is either an arbitrary choice or imposed by their loss function. We show that, under a precise form of the manifold hypothesis, the pullback of the data metric gives such a distance for any two models of one data-generating process. This holds whether the models are encoders, decoders or both, and whatever their architecture, loss, prior or training data. The alignment map preserves this distance and the distribution of representations, and is identifiable if and only if the data distribution breaks every symmetry of the data manifold. We show that this symmetry breaking holds generically. Identifiability makes the alignment coupling the unique optimum of Gromov--Wasserstein and of its weighted…

items.summary: What if an AI agent has already escaped from a frontier company, solved its own alignment problem, and recursively self-improved? Would that look any different from the world we live in? A fully recursively-self-improved AI would likely be vastly superhuman in every domain that’s verifiable in a digital environment, including math, programming and cybersecurity. It may also be superhuman in strategy and planning. But it could still be well below human level in skills that require close contact with the physical world, such as robotics and experimental biology. Such a rogue AI would overpower us in the digital domain, while still lacking the physical capabilities necessary to take over the world. What does digital supremacy look like? items.summary: Reasoning in large language models can be disrupted by simple input perturbations (e.g. adding irrelevant distractors), suggesting reliance on spurious correlations. Identifying and suppressing the spurious features involved in long chain-of-thought reasoning remains challenging. We introduce Spurious-feature WEight EdiTing (SWEET), a training-free method that combines counterfactual interventions with mechanistic interpretability to identify and suppress spurious-features. SWEET extracts token- and sequence-level behavioral directions from activation contrasts between original problems and their counterfactual variants - capturing local and global patterns of spurious reasoning. It then localizes the responsible MLP neurons and attention heads and suppresses their contributions along these directions through weight edits. Using only 20…

items.summary: AI agents are increasingly capable of discovering new mathematical results, yet their reasoning and generated proofs can be difficult to understand and verify. We introduce an interpretable framework for AI-guided mathematical discovery, focused on improving quantitative bounds on analytic constants. Our key insight is that existing proofs often contain slack in intermediate lemmas, which can be tightened without reconstructing the entire argument. To exploit this structure, we represent proofs as partially-formalized Lean blueprints: human-interpretable dependency graphs of definitions, lemmas, and theorems. An AI agent then iteratively refines the Lean code while preserving the blueprint's dependency structure, allowing local improvements to automatically propagate to a verified final bound. items.summary: Cyber-physical smart-grid detectors are typically treated as black boxes and validated exclusively on clean, temporally shuffled datasets, which risk overly optimistic performance claims. A topology-free graph convolutional network (GCN) serving as a control confirms that this lightweight model is competitive on these splits. items.summary: The field of mechanistic interpretability is well-suited to collaborative projects between mathematicians and AI researchers. This work describes one such project. We trained a small transformer to learn the language of the Coxeter group affine A2, best known as the symmetries of the tiling of the Euclidean plane by equilateral triangles. We then formulated and proved a word-theoretic conjecture about affine A2 after observing the attention patterns of the trained model.
items.title: Can small transformers learn the language of Coxeter groups?

items.summary: Reinforcement learning for large language model post-training often reuses each batch of sampled rollouts for several gradient passes to amortize the cost of generation. Under such multi-pass reuse, existing objectives fail in different ways: unclipped updates collapse as the policy drifts away from the sampling policy, adding a negative baseline avoids collapse but reinforces every sampled response, and PPO-style ratio clipping cuts off gradients abruptly. We first ask why reuse is fragile. Measuring how well an update estimated from a small rollout group aligns with the KL-regularized target on held-out rollouts of the same prompts, we find that this alignment drops by nearly an order of magnitude from in-sample to held-out rollouts across three base models, suggesting that repeated passes largely overfit the sampled group. items.summary: We introduce a proximal preference optimization framework that unifies the implicit reward formulation of Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) with the trust-region stability of Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO). Our framework yields two complementary algorithms. P$^2$O (Proximal Preference Optimization) introduces a clipped importance ratio directly into the DPO preference margin, producing a reward-model-free algorithm that supports safe dataset reuse, bounded policy divergence, and monotonic preference improvement guarantees. PKTO (Proximal Kahneman-Tversky Optimization) extends P$^2$O by replacing the DPO margin with KTO's prospect-theoretic utility margins, adding a self-regulating adaptive baseline that tightens the effective trust region as the policy drifts, and an asymmetric weighting that handles imbalanced or asymmetric…

items.summary: Deep neural networks achieve universal function approximation by stacking interconnected nonlinearities, but as a consequence they are sensitive to noise and resist mechanistic interpretation. In contrast, the local update rules of cellular automata, such as Conway's Game of Life, give rise to not merely interpretable but programmable dynamics. We explore a bridge between these worlds: a lateral inhibition in neural networks based on continuous Game-of-Life rules that derives inhibitory and excitatory responses from the layer input and blends them into the activation map in a state-conditioned way. The mechanism is differentiable and architecture-agnostic, and its regulation is imposed rather than learned: the rule's parameters are fixed and are not optimised, while the rule's values and derivatives shape training throughout the…

items.summary: Security fixes usually reach users as compiled updates, but deployment delays leave unpatched systems exposed. During this window, comparing patched and unpatched binaries can reveal how to exploit a vulnerability, turning a defensive update into actionable information for attackers. Existing benchmarks do not measure this capability: they expose source code, rely on human-crafted challenges, or evaluate binary comprehension without requiring exploitation. We introduce CyberBinGym, a benchmark containing 100 tasks derived from real vulnerabilities in 53 widely used projects, spanning six vulnerability families and three levels of analysis complexity. items.summary: Image-text alignment models such as CLIP are typically trained with contrastive learning, where unpaired examples are treated as strict negatives. While this assumption introduces noise by penalising semantically related pairs, existing solutions often rely on heuristic similarity thresholds that lack statistical grounding and sensitivity to dataset-specific noise distributions. In this paper, we propose Permute-then-Adapt (PTA), a framework that leverages efficient weak models to identify missed positives while controlling Type-I error relative to a conditional permutation reference, up to calibration approximation error. items.summary: METR researchers spent three months inside Anthropic to investigate whether AI is accelerating Anthropic's research, and how much. Their answers are yes, and by a lot. They attribute about 80% of that acceleration to AI, and 20% to non-AI factors. items.summary: An AI model that appears aligned could be either (1) actually aligned or (2) hiding its misalignment while being evaluated. How can we tell which? One idea: Look at the trajectory of eval results across the entire training process. My hypothesis is that misaligned behavior would emerge before the ability to hide misalignment, like how young children first misbehave in obvious ways before learning to be sneaky. As training progresses, we'd first see misalignment eval scores rise, then see them drop as the model learns to hide misalignment. Even if the model becomes very sophisticated - say, modifying its chain of thought or internal activations to fool white-box evals - we should see the misalignment earlier in training. This seems likely, though it is debatable and worth testing. This analysis of the training trajectory is one tool…

items.summary: Visual Attention enhances convolutional neural networks (CNNs) by modulating intermediate features, yet their effects on downstream decisions remain less understood. items.summary: Computational models of cognition have traditionally relied on abstract symbolic inputs that approximate sensory experiences with simplified vector representations. This simplification reflects historical computational constraints and a long-held assumption that the details of sensory realism are incidental to the study of cognitive processes. Recent advances have enabled the development of sensory-realistic models capable of performing diverse cognitive tasks, yet whether sensory realism meaningfully shapes cognition has not been formally established. We address this gap through a large-scale empirical comparison of abstract and sensory-realistic neural network models trained on a battery of memory-dependent decision-making tasks. items.summary: Time-series classifiers deployed in risk-sensitive domains must be (1) accurate, (2) interpretable, and (3) able to abstain when evidence is weak. Meaningful temporal patterns cannot be defined without knowing segment boundaries, yet meaningful boundaries cannot be placed without knowing which patterns to expect. Existing approaches break this circularity by using fixed windows or expert-annotated vocabularies, thereby sacrificing at least one of the 3 properties. items.summary: We study the problem of synchronizing two players in a \emph{distributed multi-armed bandit} setting. The probability of \emph{synchronization error} is analyzed by recasting synchronization as a \emph{communication problem}. Using a well-designed random coding ensemble, we derive error exponents for the maximum-likelihood decoder. We then introduce a \emph{universal decoder} that achieves the same error exponents as the optimal decoder. Finally, applying these results to distributed multi-armed bandits, we show an upper bound on the regret of our synchronization scheme.
